correctness.rationale: The proof exhausts subalgebras by projection to the three-dimensional Heisenberg quotient and intersection with its two-dimensional center. The only projection dimensions are 0,1,2,3. Two-dimensional quotient subalgebras must contain the central quotient generator and have a forced one-dimensional central bracket, while full quotient projection forces the entire center. The graph-lift counts q^{a(2-k)} are exact, with characteristic-two alternation handled. Independent RREF bracket-closure enumeration over F2,F3,F4 matches every coefficient and the abelian/nonabelian split. Finite computation is supplementary; algebraic classification proves all finite fields.

value.rationale: This is a complete dimension-refined subalgebra count for the first free nilpotent rank-two Lie algebra beyond class two, directly complementary to published ideal counts of the identical natural object. The distinction is structural: nonabelian 3D Heisenberg subalgebras outnumber abelian ones by a factor growing with q, and almost all uniformly sampled subalgebras have dimensions one or two. It is not merely an arbitrary parameter slice, a textbook special case of the ideal result, or a numerical table; it classifies all closed subspaces for every finite field.
